caption: Newanforbi v. Meza-Gonzalez et al.
status: DISMISSED WITHOUT PREJUDICE — Request for Dismissal filed Aug. 15, 2026 (Code Civ. Proc. §581(b)(1),(c); entire action), taking the unruled-on U-Visa Certification Motion with it. [FLAGGED: no successor docket carries the state-law theories or the State/CHP defendant forward — see risk field.]
defendants: Santiago Meza-Gonzalez; Jose Melano; State of California / CHP; DOES 1-10
key_facts: Parallel state tort action from same Nov. 1, 2024 CHP encounter. Bane Act claim targets coerced waiver of PAS refusal right. Fabricated report constitutes independent wrongfulness. U-visa certification motion: Plaintiff seeks judicial certification under 8 U.S.C. § 1101(a)(15)(U) and Cal. Pen. Code § 679.10, establishing victim status and helpfulness in detection/investigation of qualifying criminal activity (false imprisonment, unlawful restraint, obstruction of justice, perjury, felonious assault).
procedural_status: Filed 02/04/2026. Fee Waiver Hearing 03/03/2026. CMC 07/06/2026. Mar. 25, 2026: State of California/CHP and Melano served. Meza-Gonzalez service in progress; court-ordered extension to May 4, 2026. Apr. 2, 2026: DAG Allen Haiyang Li (DOJ) notified anticipated demurrer under CCP §430.10(c) (other action pending — federal case 2:25-cv-01460-DC-CSK) and (e) (insufficient facts). M&C required per CCP §430.41; call scheduled Apr. 9, 2026. Apr. 9, 2026: M&C call completed. Li agreed in principle to stipulated stay of Alameda action pending Judge Kim's federal MTD ruling; demurrer briefing deferred. Plaintiff also raised 28 U.S.C. § 636(c) magistrate consent; Li to consult clients. Apr. 13, 2026: DAG Li circulated draft stipulation. Plaintiff reviewed and returned counter-draft same day with four additions: (1) definition of 'final resolution' tied to entry of final judgment or dispositive order plus expiration of any appeal period; (2) tolling provision for applicable statutory deadlines during stay; (3) fallback response deadline if parties cannot agree after stay lifts; (4) without-prejudice clause preserving all claims, defenses, and rights. Apr. 14, 2026 (11:32 AM): Li accepted all counter-draft language without further revision and placed stipulation on pleading paper. Plaintiff reviewed, signed, and returned executed copy (Apr. 14, 12:03 PM). Apr. 14, 2026 (1:50 PM): Adriana Zagal (DOJ Legal Secretary) served filed copies via E-SERVICE — Stipulation for Stay Pending Resolution of Concurrent Federal Action and [Proposed] Order re: Stipulation for Stay. Action is now STAYED in its entirety pending final resolution of federal Matter 1 (2:25-cv-01460-DC-CSK). All discovery and deadlines suspended; no claims, defenses, or rights waived. June 2026: U-Visa Certification Motion briefed — filed after CHP Commander Serrato's April 20, 2026 denial of Petitioner's direct certification request (the same denial challenged by mandamus in Matter 20); this motion asks the Alameda Superior Court judge already presiding over this tort action to certify Form I-918 Supplement B directly, as an independent, parallel track to Matter 20's writ compelling CHP itself to certify. June 5, 2026: Defendants (State/CHP/Meza-Gonzalez/Melano) filed Opposition, arguing U-visa certification requires pending criminal prosecution, that a civil judge has no role certifying victims of crimes alleged only in a civil complaint, and disputing the Motion's citation to 8 C.F.R. §214.14(a)(14)(ii) as unsupported by the subsection's actual text. June 8, 2026: Plaintiff filed a 12-page Reply: (1) clarified that the 'no prosecution required' proposition rests on 8 C.F.R. §214.14(a)(12) and USCIS's U Visa Law Enforcement Resource Guide, not (a)(14)(ii) — conceding the citation but not the underlying point, and noting Defendants' own quoted text from (a)(14)(ii) (obstruction/perjury victims harmed by 'manipulation of the legal system') independently supports certification on this record; (2) argued 8 U.S.C. §1101(a)(15)(U)(i)(III) and Cal. Penal Code §679.10(a)(1) both list judges among certifying officials without limiting that role to criminal proceedings, and that CHP's own refusal to certify is precisely why judicial certification exists; (3) tied the qualifying offenses to record evidence — the dashcam's 'Is it water? No this is piss' exchange (obstruction/perjury re: the warrant affidavit), the Nov. 1–5, 2024 confinement (false imprisonment), and the warrantless blood draw (felonious assault/battery). Hearing held June 18, 2026 at 2:30 p.m. in Dept. 518 before Hon. Mark Fickes; no ruling was ever reported. Note: the underlying Motion for U-Visa Certification itself (only the Opposition and Reply) is not currently hosted in this repository's document store. Separately, on the CM-110 (originally due Jun. 3, 2026) and the Jul. 6, 2026 CMC referenced in the timeline: both postdate the Apr. 14, 2026 stay stipulation, whose own text ('Action is now STAYED in its entirety... All discovery and deadlines suspended') unambiguously covers them — both are superseded by the stay and did not need to be met. Aug. 15, 2026: Request for Dismissal Without Prejudice (Aug. 11, 2026 draft, pending CIV-110 transcription) filed under CCP §581(b)(1),(c), dismissing the action and the unruled U-Visa Motion. Terminates the state-law theories and State/CHP defendant; see risk field.
damages: $100,000 - $300,000+ historical claim, now dismissed with no successor docket [FLAGGED: (1) no breakdown reserved or excluded the CDL lost-wage component already claimed in Matters 1, 7, and 20 for the same one-year suspension — see the same note on Matter 1's damages field; (2) the False Imprisonment/Battery/Bane Act components of this figure are not pled anywhere else in the portfolio as of the Aug. 15, 2026 dismissal — confirm intentional abandonment or refile before the Nov. 1, 2026 CCP §335.1 backstop]
risk: Terminal — dismissed Aug. 15, 2026.
